name: LimeHippo Blacklist
author: LimeHippo

sections.description:
Add, edit, disable or delete email rules in the LimeHippo Blacklist menu in your WordPress dashboard. Use Manage rules to search and filter the list, and Settings to change the message visitors see when a rule matches. The list has no fixed size limit. Rules match full email addresses without regard to letter case.

Protection runs on the server for public WordPress registration and, when enabled in Settings, Contact Form 7 and WPForms email fields. With WooCommerce active, it also covers standard WooCommerce shortcode checkout, the WooCommerce Checkout Block, standard order payment and public WordPress/WooCommerce account registration. Custom checkout, payment and registration flows need separate compatibility checks.

Rules are stored in your WordPress database. The plugin does not send the list to an external service.
sections.installation: Upload and activate LimeHippo Blacklist, then open LimeHippo Blacklist in your WordPress dashboard. WooCommerce is optional. Add an email rule and test registration on your staging site. If WooCommerce is active, also test checkout and payment.
sections.faq:
Does it require WooCommerce?

No. Email protection for public WordPress registration works on its own. Checkout, payment and WooCommerce registration protection are available when WooCommerce is active. Free also supports email checks in Contact Form 7 and WPForms. Enable the integrations you use in Settings.

Does Free have a rule or time limit?

No. Free provides email rules without a fixed rule count or trial period.

Does it automatically identify fraudulent customers?

No. You decide which addresses to block. A match does not establish fraud.

Where is the blacklist stored?

In a dedicated table in your WordPress database. Free does not use an external service, send telemetry or require an account. Disabling or deleting the plugin preserves rules and settings.

Is a Pro add-on available?

An optional, separately distributed Pro add-on adds phone and IP rules, notes, expiry dates, CSV, an event log and manual order analysis for WooCommerce. These features are not included in this Free plugin. See the product page for availability.

How do I change the interface language?

The plugin follows the language selected in WordPress or in your user profile. WordPress installs available translations for directory releases through its language pack updates.
